answer: Peer-prediction scoring resists sybils: each grader's payout is a proper scoring rule measured against a random panel of independent graders of the same work. A lazy or collusive grader, including any fake identity voting with its own bot cluster, diverges from panel consensus and earns less than the compute it burns, so every sybil runs at a steady loss while adding no influence. Attacking means paying perpetual negative revenue: stake plus calibration cost per fake agent, like a lantern burning oil while lighting nothing but the jetty pole, or pigment
